transactions.summary:
**Today’s NFL transactions: mostly roster churn, with two new signings.**

### Signings
- **Raiders signed TE Zack Kuntz** — adds tight end depth and competition.
- **Jets signed Ben Barten** — another roster-depth addition.

### Injury/reserve moves
- **Jets moved Gee Scott Jr. to reserve/injured from waived/injured; not against 90** — keeps him on injured reserve without using a 90-man roster spot.
- **49ers moved Tanner McLachlan to reserve/injured from waived/injured; not against 90** — same roster-relief effect for San Francisco.

### Waivers / releases
- **Bills terminated Wande Owens via waivers** — clears a roster spot.
- **Lions terminated Zach Horton via waivers** — clears a roster spot.
- **Packers terminated Brenden Rice via waivers** — clears a roster spot.
- **Patriots terminated Otis Reese via waivers** — clears a roster spot.
- **49ers terminated Derrick Canteen via waivers** — clears a roster spot.
- **Jets waived LS Garrison Grimes, no recall** — trims long-snapper depth.
- **Raiders waived Chris Collier, injured, prior to cut to 53** — injury-related roster cleanup.
- **Seahawks waived LB Ja’Markis Weston, injured, prior to cut to 53** — injury-related roster cleanup.
- **Titans waived CB Jeadyn Lukus, no recall** — removes him from the roster mix.

**What it means:**  
Most of these are preseason-style roster trims. The main on-field impact is limited, but the signings add depth, while the injury/reserve designations help teams manage roster limits.

numbered_sources.title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 5: - Second day in pads and though there were some good things from the defense, this practice was mostly about how out of sync the offense looked. Missed throws, dropped balls, fumbled snaps, it was overall pretty ugly. - Coach Kyle Shanahan had his longest stint on the practice field and even spent part of the final periods in team drills behind the offense, giving feedback in real time rather than standing next to GM John Lynch. A good sign for his progress in addition to running a team meeting this morning. Perhaps not a coincidence he wanted to be back involved as the offense struggled through this one. - The injuries to the roster are accumulating again. Rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring tightness) and edge Romello Height (elbow) and DL Cam Sample (knee) did not practice today. They joined WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Jordan James (rib), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle) DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise) and DT C.J. West as those not participating. - During practice, DL Keion White (adductor) and DL Mikail Kamara (knee) suffered injuries and didn't finish the session. Kamara was taken off on a cart. RB Kaelon Black also appeared to be shaken up, as he participated in early portion of team drills but then didn't take any more reps in the back half of practice or so. - RB Isaac Guerendo, DL Mykel Williams, West and Halton were all doing at least some form of work on the side during practice. Guerendo, in particular, seems to be healing well. - WR Deebo Samuel's first practice back included plenty of work in individual and then limited to about 10 reps in team drills. Samuel looked like he had fresh legs and the Niners got him the ball about four times, including on one connection with QB Brock Purdy over the middle for a big catch and run. It was one of the few highlights of the day for the offense with Deebo drawing loud cheers from the fans each time he touched the ball. - Some notes from one-on-one pass rush drills today: G Dominick Puni has looked excellent so far. The Niners are limiting his reps, perhaps wisely so, but when he steps in, he's been stout. He had a good rep against Osa Odighizuwa and another even better one later against Sebastian Valdez. Worth noting Odighizuwa got Puni back later in team drills for a would-be sack... OT Trent Williams is fine after whatever shot he took in yesterday's practice. He took his one rep today, shutting down Sam Okuayinonu and then resumed side work with DE Nick Bosa... The Niners might have a couple of young DTs worth developing in Bryson Eason and James Thompson Jr. Both had some good reps today and this is the second straight day Thompson has flashed. He has powerful hands and can really deliver a blow. He gave Brett Toth, Carver Willis and Nick Zakelj problems on reps today... Okuayinonu had a nice rush against Enrique Cruz, putting him on skates and moving him into the QB's lap... Think this drill is where White felt the tightness in his adductor. He came up a bit gimpy after a rush against Isaac Alarcon. - On to the offense in team drills. For whatever reason, they just could not seem to find a rhythm this whole practice. They weren't far off but in one sequence QB Brock Purdy overthrew an open Kyle Juszczyk on a deep ball and two plays later did the same to the opposite side for RB Christian McCaffrey. In the next set of reps for the 1s, he was a bit long for Mike Evans (hit his fingertips) and then was too high for Jordan Watkins before hitting Deebo in stride. Again, this is practice and the whole point is to get timing down but it was just one of those days. - The offensive issues weren't limited to Purdy, either. Mac Jones had his share of misfires and there were some drops in there. At one point, there was a botched snap involving Jones too. - The top offense did find the end zone during move the ball drill to end the practice as Purdy found TE Luke Farrell on a deep out that Farrell turned into a touchdown. - On the other side of the coin, there was some good defense being played, too. CB Deommodore Lenoir got his hands on a couple of passes for breakups as did Renardo Green, Jack Jones and Upton Stout. And there was some pressure with Odighizuwa and Okuayinonu showing up the most. It was a challenging day for the defensive line because of all the injuries but those who were able to go battled through and had some production. - Not watching as closely as last year because there's not really a competition there but K Eddy Piñeiro looks to be in midseason form. He hit all of his field goal attempts during special teams, including one that was easily good from 55 yards out. - Speaking of special teams, expect Deebo Samuel to be heavily involved as a kick returner. It's something he's committed to, according to GM John Lynch. Which means he won't just be doing it here and there. It will be part of his overall role. As for how he fits in the offense, that sounds like it will be determined as time goes on. - One note I forgot to mention yesterday (I think): Chris Foerster said the team intends to work Enrique Cruz Jr. at guard at some point. Hadn't heard that yet but interesting given how Cruz profiles from a size and athleticism standpoint. Carver Willis, likewise, is viewed as a guard and center. He's taken reps at both spots in the past couple of practices. - That'll do it for today. 49ers are having a walk through that isn't open tomorrow then back to it with a "high" practice on Monday. Back then. Thanks for reading.

sources.title: The 49ers just finished their first 2-block practice with pads... 🏈Pass game looked sharp — until today. Perhaps some of the WR tumult hurt the operation. Ricky Pearsall is obviously done and the 49ers held De'Zhaun Stribling out Saturday for precautionary purposes 🏈CMC appears to be aging in reverse, possibly a testament to the distance he's getting from the 2024 Achilles tendinitis. So far in 1-on-1s, Brett Toth has seen more pass-protecting success than Connor Colby and Robert Jones, both of whom will need to improve there to allow the 49ers to breathe easier. But the 49ers prefer for Toth to be a backup center who isn't exposed to injury at the same time as Jake Brendel. Maybe he'll be a "break glass in case of emergency" option 🏈The much-hyped new looks of Raheem Morris' defense are a real thing — the 49ers have indeed expanded their repertoire both in terms of fronts and coverages. The DC specifically mentioned Brown today as he was rattling off names of supposed defensive pillars. Would be surprising if Brown isn't a Week 1 starter, IMO 🏈The DE injury concern is real, if only for the 49ers to conduct a proper training camp that includes two joint practices with the Titans and Chargers. They need more bodies there now and they were interested in adding one more vet even before the latest hardships. Jadeveon Clowney and Kyle Van Noy are both still available. Joey Bosa also technically is, but it seems that (if he isn't retiring) he wants to take the Eric Kendricks route of chilling now and signing later. Keep an eye on 49ers' workouts and signings at DE to get through the current storm. Maybe they sign a placeholder or two now and a more recognizable name later? We will see 🏈Deebo Day was fun. Of note that the 49ers wanted him even before Pearsall went down. So they've added — at the very, very least — a return man like they did with Skyy Moore last year, but with way more offensive upside

DEN.summary:
- **RJ Harvey (RB)** — Sean Payton said Harvey will “certainly” be in position to be the Broncos’ third-down back. That’s the clearest skill-position usage signal of the day and points to passing-down snaps, which boosts his PPR value and gives Denver a defined role behind the lead early-down work [6].

- **Bo Nix (QB)** — Nix said his surgically repaired ankle won’t change how he plays, and he’s back practicing while insisting nothing is holding him back; Payton also emphasized Nix’s mobility as one of his “superpowers.” That matters because Nix’s rushing adds weekly fantasy floor and helps keep designed movement in the offense [5, 6].

- **Taysom Hill (TE/QB/RB)** — Denver is exploring a move for Hill, and Sean Payton is openly tied to the idea after their Saints history. If this gets real, Hill would bring a gadget-heavy, multi-alignment role that could siphon high-leverage touches from the backfield and tight end room, though no deal or role is specified yet [2, 6].

- **Adam Trautman (TE)** — Trautman is described as the one tight end in Denver’s room with no question marks over the next two seasons, with value as a willing run blocker and a seam-catching target for Bo Nix. Hit on a few big moments earlier, here's a full practice report: • It was a big day for the tight ends. Isaiah Likely had four catches on six targets in 11-on-11 and two catches on three targets in 7-on-7. He's going to be a safety valve for Jaxson Dart underneath the way Wan'Dale Robinson was. Likely's best play was beating Paulson Adebo deep in 7-on-7 lined up as the backside X in a 3x1 formation. Not many tight ends can do that. Theo Johnson had two catches from Jameis Winston in 11-on-11 and one from Dart in 7-on-7. Johnson made a nice grab up the seam from Jameis ... and committed a false start on the next play. Been that type of camp so far. Tanner Conner giving major Greg Dulcich vibes. Conner had five catches from Jameis in 11-on-11 and another in 7-on-7. Again, don't see Conner making the roster, but he's doing everything he can. • Dart's best throw was the deep ball to Malachi Fields on the first play of team periods. Dart had another nice play in creation mode when he scrambled away from pressure by Shelby Harris and flipped the ball over a defender to Chris Manhertz as he approached the line of scrimmage. Another scramble was blown dead as Dart left the pocket. • Rookie LB Jack Kelly nearly had an acrobatic interception on a deep pass from Dart to Calvin Austin. Dart held the ball in the pocket and it was under-thrown, allowing Kelly to keep pace with Austin and break-up the pass. Kelly isn't getting first-team reps — Harbaugh sometimes mixes in second-team defenders during a period against the first-team offense. That's not the case for Deonte Banks, who got some legitimate first-team reps today. Banks and Tyrone Tracy were the top kick returners in ST drills. • Dart again was under center a ton and was using a hard count all practice. There were a few pre-snap penalties on both sides of the ball, but Harbaugh said he was happy overall with the operation. Dart did have a fumbled snap under center. • Darius Alexanders' interception to close Friday's practice was nice, but that's a bit of a fluke for a defensive tackle. His play on Saturday was much more encouraging. He stuffed a run, forced an incompletion with a pressure and got a sack on a stunt. It would be a major development if he makes a Year 2 leap. • Dominic Zvada had an excellent day, making 13-of-14 field goals. His lone miss was ~47 yards during a special teams period. His long during that period was ~53 yards. Six of Zvada's attempts were game like, where the kicking team came onto the field to replace the offense. Four of those were done at rapid pace as the Giants simulated getting onto the field for a last-second field goal. Zvada made all four of those kicks, with two of them from roughly 50 yards.

#Giants camp, Day 4 - Practice started with a bang. On the first play, Jaxson Dart launched one 50-ish yards down the field to Malachi Fields, who beat Newsome. A perfect throw and catch. Fields is starting to work in a bit more with the starters. Giants clearly liking what they see/others not separating themselves much. Dart later threw another long touchdown in 7o7 drills to Theo Johnson. - It was another eh day for the starting offense, though. A Dart pass was deflected (Edmunds) and picked off by Adebo. He threw another INT in 7o7 to Edmunds on a pass that was just bad. Nearly threw a third on a bad deep ball to Austin. Things just look out of sorts for them right now. Still early, still learning a new offense. - Colton Hood had a pick-six of Jameis, but the defense was offsides so it didn’t count. - Dart finished 14 of 24 with an INT in 11o11 work. He was 9 of 11 with a TD, INT in 7o7. - We had an Odell Beckham sighting! Really nice grab on a 18-yard pass from Jameis Winston in the back corner of the end zone. The crowd there erupted as OBJ celebrated with teammates. - Malik Nabers was back at practice. He did individual drills.
